```{r read-in-abstracts}
#read in the abstracts you previously retrieved with the Hunnicutt_Schumer_2026_Retrieve_Hybridization_PubMed_Abstracts.md script; confirm number of entries is 12282 (accurate as of 2Feb26)
pmids <- read.table("data/hybridization_MESH_terms_pubmed_search_2Feb26.txt")
num_pmids <- dim(pmids)[1]

# efetch limits the number of queries that can be submitted at one time so the PubMed IDs (PMIDs) need to be split into batches; have chosen a batch size of 100 here
batch_size <- 100
num_batches <- ceiling(num_pmids / batch_size)

# create a data frame of the start and end abstract for each batch
batches <- NULL
for (batch in 1:num_batches){
  if(batch < num_batches){
    batch_bounds <- c(((batch-1)*batch_size)+1, batch*batch_size)
  } else {
    batch_bounds <- c(((batch-1)*batch_size)+1, num_pmids)
  }
  batches <- rbind(batches, t(data.frame(batch_bounds)))
}
batches <- unname(batches)
```

```{r begin-parsing-and-fetch abstracts}
# read in saved abstract .rds file
full_metadata_df <- readRDS(file = "data/all_abstracts_2Feb26.rds")

#split the pub date into day, month, year columns
full_metadata_df <- separate(full_metadata_df, grep("date", colnames(full_metadata_df)), into = c("day", "month", "year"), sep = "-", remove = FALSE)
dim(full_metadata_df)

#remove papers with no abstract
full_noMiss_metadata_df <- full_metadata_df[!is.na(full_metadata_df$abstract),]
dim(full_noMiss_metadata_df)

#some titles import with brackets; remove those brackets
full_noMiss_metadata_df$title <- gsub("^\\[", "", full_noMiss_metadata_df$title)
full_noMiss_metadata_df$title <- gsub("\\]$", "", full_noMiss_metadata_df$title)

#append PMID to abstract; the scientific name parser (gnfinder) prefers to be run only once on the entire dataset; by appending the PMID to the abstract text, we can then backtrace mentions of scientific names to the abstracts/PMIDs they belong to
full_noMiss_metadata_df$abstract_wID <- paste("[[DOC:", 
                                              full_noMiss_metadata_df$pmid, "]] ", 
                                              full_noMiss_metadata_df$title, " ",
                                              full_noMiss_metadata_df$abstract,
                                              sep = "")
#append abstracts together for gnfinder run
abstracts_for_gnfinder <- paste(full_noMiss_metadata_df$abstract_wID, collapse = "\n")

#occasionally authors will not include spaces when describing crosses and this interferes with gnfinder; forcibly adds spaces after and before hyphens
abstracts_for_gnfinder <- gsub("-", " - ", abstracts_for_gnfinder)

#create a table of start and end positions of each abstract using the appended PMIDs from above
full_noMiss_metadata_df$start_pos <- gregexpr("\\[\\[DOC", abstracts_for_gnfinder)[[1]]
full_noMiss_metadata_df$end_pos <- c((gregexpr("\\[\\[DOC", abstracts_for_gnfinder)[[1]][-1]-1), nchar(abstracts_for_gnfinder))

# run gnfinder on all abstracts at once; using the arguments -s 11 and -f to use GBIF as the source database to verify matches against
tsv <- system2(
  "gnfinder",
  args = c("-s","11","-U","-v","-f", "tsv"),
  input = abstracts_for_gnfinder,
  stdout = TRUE
)

# import gnfinder dataframe of detected scientific names
abstract_df <- read.table(text = tsv, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#attach PMIDs to each entry
setDT(abstract_df)
setDT(full_noMiss_metadata_df)

abstract_df <- abstract_df[full_noMiss_metadata_df,
                           pmid := i.pmid,
                           on = .(Start > start_pos, Start < end_pos)]


#split identified scientific names into two categories; one is for good matches that don't need to be altered; the other is for potential scientific names where the genus is abbreviated
abstract_df_good_matches <- abstract_df[!grepl("\\.", abstract_df$Name) & !abstract_df$VerifMatchType == "NoMatch",]
abstract_df_abbreviated <- abstract_df[grepl("\\.", abstract_df$Name) & abstract_df$VerifMatchType == "NoMatch",]
```

```{r substitute-candidate-genera-for-abbreviations}
# now that we have our list of candidate genera for each abstract, we need to fine tune the potential abbreviated species names; gnfinder search parameters meant that some common words were returned across potential scientific names; here we are removing those terms from the abbreviated names
```

```{r occurrence-lookup}
# get counts of occurrences in different countries for each species
get_occurrence_data <- function(taxon) {
  # get GBIF species name corresponding to givne taxon
  key <- name_usage_key_df_species[taxon,]$speciesKey
  species <- name_usage_key_df_species[taxon,]$species
  
  # gather all country occurrence data with no GeospatialIssues for each taxon
  tmp_counts <- occ_count(taxonKey=name_usage_key_df_species$speciesKey[taxon], 
                          occurrenceStatus = "PRESENT", 
                          hasGeospatialIssue = FALSE,
                          facet = "country", facetLimit=250)
  
  # if there are any occurrence records
  if(dim(tmp_counts)[1] > 0) {
    
    # make a dataframe for each taxon containing the species, the number of countries it was observed in (this is important for later to weed out widespread species), record the country with the most and second most occurrence records, as well as the number of records for each
    df <- data.frame(key = key,
                     species = species, 
                     num_countries = dim(tmp_counts)[1],
                     top_country = as.character(tmp_counts[1,1]),
                     top_country_count = as.numeric(tmp_counts[1,2]),
                     second_country = as.character(tmp_counts[2,1]),
                     second_country_count = as.numeric(tmp_counts[2,2]))
    
  } else {
    # if there are no occurrence records, set all the occurrence data to zero in the taxon-specific dataframe
    df <- data.frame(key = key,
                     species = species, 
                     num_countries = 0,
                     top_country = NA,
                     top_country_count = 0,
                     second_country = NA,
                     second_country_count = 0)
  }
  return(df)
}

# #apply the get_occurrence_data function to all taxa with a good species name; this takes a while to run; uncomment if you have never run this before
# occurrence_data_list <- lapply(1:nrow(name_usage_key_df_species), get_occurrence_data)
# 
# # rbind all occurrence data into one data frame and reduce duplicates
# occurrence_data_df <- do.call(rbind, occurrence_data_list)
# occurrence_data_df$key <- as.character(occurrence_data_df$key)
# occurrence_data_df <- distinct(occurrence_data_df)
# 
# #save occurrence data
# saveRDS(occurrence_data_df, file = "data/occurrence_data_df_2Feb26.rds")

#read in occurrence data if the above chunk has been run before
occurrence_data_df <- readRDS(file = "data/occurrence_data_df_2Feb26.rds")

#now we need to eliminate widespread species; we do this in two ways
#first we eliminate species where there is a negligible difference in occurrence records between the country with the most records and the country with the second most records
occurrence_data_df$diff_in_top_occ <- (occurrence_data_df$top_country_count - occurrence_data_df$second_country_count)/
  (occurrence_data_df$top_country_count + occurrence_data_df$second_country_count)
occurrence_data_df[is.na(occurrence_data_df$diff_in_top_occ),]$diff_in_top_occ <- 0

# quick plot to confirm that there is a correlation between the number of countries a species has occurrence data in and the relative difference in occurrence records between the top and second place country
ggplot(occurrence_data_df, aes(x = num_countries, y = diff_in_top_occ)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# the second method for filtering out widespread species; remove species that don't have a good country label assigned, that were observed in more than 50 countries, and where the difference between the top two countries was less than 25%
occurrence_data_filtered_df <- occurrence_data_df[occurrence_data_df$top_country != "ZZ" &
                                                    (occurrence_data_df$num_countries < 50 | 
                                                       occurrence_data_df$diff_in_top_occ > 0.25),]

# quick plot to confirm that the filtered species no longer contain these extremely widespread species
ggplot(occurrence_data_filtered_df, aes(x = num_countries, y = diff_in_top_occ)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 
```

```{r pre-and-post-genomics-era-analysis}
# Now that we have our species records for each PMID, we want to investigate how the genomics sequencing revolution has changed hybridization research
# to begin, choose a year to split the data for pre/post-next gen sequencing comparisons
trend_year <- 2015

# add species metadata info + PMID to combined list of identified scientific names
all_matches_with_metadata <- merge(all_matches_combined, name_usage_key_df, by.x = "taxon_id", by.y = "key")
# also add publication metadata
all_matches_with_metadata <- merge(all_matches_with_metadata, full_noMiss_metadata_df, by = "pmid")

#remove non-animals
all_matches_with_metadata <- all_matches_with_metadata[all_matches_with_metadata$kingdom == "Animalia",]
dim(distinct(all_matches_with_metadata))

# merge species metadata with occurrence data
all_matches_combined_species_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[grep(" ", all_matches_with_metadata$new_name),]
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_species_level))

all_matches_with_metadata_with_occurrence_data <- merge(all_matches_with_metadata, occurrence_data_filtered_df, by.x = "taxon_id", by.y = "key")
dim(distinct(all_matches_with_metadata_with_occurrence_data))

# create species level metadata
all_matches_combined_species_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[!is.na(all_matches_with_metadata$species),]
all_matches_combined_species_level <- all_matches_combined_species_level[,c("species", "pmid", "year")]
all_matches_combined_species_level <- distinct(all_matches_combined_species_level)
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_species_level))

#quick check of the top species before and after the genomics cut-off year; we can see that Drosophila, Mus, and Bos dominate these lists
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_species_level[all_matches_combined_species_level$year < trend_year,]$species), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_species_level[all_matches_combined_species_level$year > trend_year,]$species), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)

# create genus level metadata
all_matches_combined_genus_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[!is.na(all_matches_with_metadata$genus),]
all_matches_combined_genus_level <- all_matches_combined_genus_level[,c("genus", "pmid", "year")]
all_matches_combined_genus_level <- distinct(all_matches_combined_genus_level)
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_genus_level))

#quick check of the top genera before and after the genomics cut-off year; we can see that Drosophila melanogaster and simulans, Mus musculus, and Bos taurus dominate these lists
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_genus_level[all_matches_combined_genus_level$year < trend_year,]$genus), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_genus_level[all_matches_combined_genus_level$year > trend_year,]$genus), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)

# create family level metadata
all_matches_combined_family_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[!is.na(all_matches_with_metadata$family),]
all_matches_combined_family_level <- all_matches_combined_family_level[,c("family", "pmid", "year")]
all_matches_combined_family_level <- distinct(all_matches_combined_family_level)
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_family_level))

#quick check of the top genera before and after the genomics cut-off year; we can see that Drosophilidae and Muridae dominate before genomics, and that both drop in the post-genomics era
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_family_level[all_matches_combined_family_level$year < trend_year,]$family), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_family_level[all_matches_combined_family_level$year > trend_year,]$family), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)

# create order level metadata
all_matches_combined_order_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[!is.na(all_matches_with_metadata$order),]
all_matches_combined_order_level <- all_matches_combined_order_level[,c("order", "pmid", "year")]
all_matches_combined_order_level <- distinct(all_matches_combined_order_level)
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_order_level))

#quick check of the top orders pre- and post-genomics era
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_order_level[all_matches_combined_order_level$year < trend_year,]$order), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_order_level[all_matches_combined_order_level$year > trend_year,]$order), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)

# create class level metadata
all_matches_combined_class_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[!is.na(all_matches_with_metadata$class),]
all_matches_combined_class_level <- all_matches_combined_class_level[,c("class", "pmid", "year")]
all_matches_combined_class_level <- distinct(all_matches_combined_class_level)
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_class_level))

#quick check of the top orders pre- and post-genomics era; Insecta and Mammalia (driven by Mus and Drosophila) reign pre-genomics but then Actinopterygii and Aves make great strides post-genomics
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_class_level[all_matches_combined_class_level$year < trend_year,]$class), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_class_level[all_matches_combined_class_level$year > trend_year,]$class), decreasing = TRUE), n = 10)

# create phylum level metadata
all_matches_combined_phylum_level <- all_matches_with_metadata[!is.na(all_matches_with_metadata$phylum),]
all_matches_combined_phylum_level <- all_matches_combined_phylum_level[,c("phylum", "pmid", "year")]
all_matches_combined_phylum_level <- distinct(all_matches_combined_phylum_level)
dim(distinct(all_matches_combined_phylum_level))

#quick check of the top phyla pre- and post-genomics era; everything is Chordata or Arthropoda; minimal change with genomics
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_phylum_level[all_matches_combined_phylum_level$year < trend_year,]$phylum), decreasing = TRUE), n = 11)
head(sort(table(all_matches_combined_phylum_level[all_matches_combined_phylum_level$year > trend_year,]$phylum), decreasing = TRUE), n = 11)
```

```{r map-occurrence-data}
#import a world map sf object
world_map <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

#filter occurrence data frame to just the countries with the most occurrence records per species
representation_df <- data.frame(table(all_matches_with_metadata_with_occurrence_data$top_country))

#make sure country codes are consistent with world map and occurrence records
colnames(representation_df) <- c("iso_a3", "country_count")
representation_df$iso2c <- countrycode(representation_df$iso_a3, 
                                       origin = "iso2c", 
                                       destination = "iso3c")

# merge data frames of world map countries and the occurrence records
map_data_merged <- merge(world_map, representation_df, by.x = "wb_a2", by.y = "iso_a3",
                         all = TRUE)

#generate the species occurrence map in Figure 1E
figure_1_species_map <- ggplot(data = map_data_merged) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = log(country_count)), color = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#D1ECE6", high = "#2A5147", na.value = "#EDEDED") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Geographic distribution of hybridization studies", 
       x = "Longitude", 
       y = "Latitude",
       fill = "log(Species count)") +
  theme_void() +
  coord_sf(crs = "ESRI:54030")

figure_1_species_map
```

```{r hybridization-timeline}
# generate the timeline of pubmed papers that mention hybridization with key papers of interest highlighted and split into the "Eras" of hybridization research discussed in the main text
key_papers <- read.csv("data/key_hybridization_papers_and_eras.csv")
eras <- key_papers[key_papers$category == "era",]
eras[eras$label == "Classic Era",]$year <- 1945
papers_only <- key_papers[key_papers$category == "paper",]
papers_only <- papers_only[papers_only$year > 1945,]

#formatting the data frame of all pubmed records
full_metadata_df$year <- as.numeric(full_metadata_df$year)

#plot histogram of hybridization papers over time for figure 1A
figure_1_publication_histogram <- ggplot(full_metadata_df[!is.na(full_metadata_df$year),],
                                         aes(x=year)) + 
  geom_histogram(color="black", fill="#9b7b97", binwidth = 1, boundary = 0) +
  geom_segment(data = papers_only, aes(x = year, y = 475, xend = year, yend = 425),
               arrow = arrow(), position = position_jitter(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_label_repel(data = papers_only, aes(x = year, y = 525, label = label),
                   max.overlaps = 20) +
  geom_rect(data = eras, aes(xmin = year + 1, xmax = end - 1, ymin = -5, ymax = -25),
            fill = "lightgray") +
  geom_text(data = eras, aes(x = (year + end)/2, y = -30, label = label)) +
  ylim(-100, 600) +
  xlim(1944, 2030) +
  labs(x = "Publication date (year)",
       y = "Number of papers published") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r phylum-pie-chart}
# generate the pie chart of represented phyla in hybridization abstracts seen in Figure 1D
phylum_counts <- data.frame(sort(table(all_matches_combined_phylum_level$phylum), decreasing = TRUE))
colnames(phylum_counts) <- c("phylum", "count")

# convert counts to coordinates for pie chart
phylum_counts <- phylum_counts %>%
  mutate(
    csum = rev(cumsum(rev(count))),
    pos = count/2 + lead(csum, 1),
    pos = if_else(is.na(pos), count/2, pos)
  )

#generate the phylum pie chart
figure_1_phylum_pie_chart <- ggplot(phylum_counts, aes(x="", y=count, fill=phylum)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", width=1) +
  coord_polar("y", start=0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#5f2321",
                               "#8b3838",
                               "#a14041",
                               "#ad6f70",
                               "#ac8f8e",
                               rep("#c2b6b7", 9))) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(y = pos, label = phylum),
    x = 1.4,
    max.overlaps = 24,
    nudge_x = 0.5,
    segment.size = 1,
    segment.color = "black",
    segment.linetype = "dotted", 
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

figure_1_phylum_pie_chart
```

```{r genus-df-generation}
# this code generates figure 1B
# calculate per-genus representation across abstracts before and after the "genomics" time split
# begin by splitting genus dataframe by the pre- and post- genomics time split

all_matches_combined_genus_level$year <- as.numeric(all_matches_combined_genus_level$year)
pre_genomics_genus_merged_df <- all_matches_combined_genus_level[
  as.numeric(all_matches_combined_genus_level$year) < trend_year &
    !is.na(all_matches_combined_genus_level$year),]
post_genomics_genus_merged_df <- all_matches_combined_genus_level[
  as.numeric(all_matches_combined_genus_level$year) > trend_year &
    !is.na(all_matches_combined_genus_level$year),]

# calculate counts of each genus within each genomics era
pre_genomics_genus <- data.frame(table(pre_genomics_genus_merged_df$genus))
colnames(pre_genomics_genus) <- c("genus", "pre_count")
post_genomics_genus <- data.frame(table(post_genomics_genus_merged_df$genus))
colnames(post_genomics_genus) <- c("genus", "post_count")

#merge pre- and post- genomics genus counts into one dataframe; set any genera not counted in one of the eras to zero
both_time_genus <- merge(pre_genomics_genus, post_genomics_genus, by = "genus", all = TRUE)
both_time_genus[is.na(both_time_genus$post_count),]$post_count <- 0
both_time_genus[is.na(both_time_genus$pre_count),]$pre_count <- 0

#convert genus counts to frequencies for each era
both_time_genus$pre_total <- sum(both_time_genus$pre_count)
both_time_genus$post_total <- sum(both_time_genus$post_count)
both_time_genus$pre_freq <- both_time_genus$pre_count/
  both_time_genus$pre_total
both_time_genus$post_freq <- both_time_genus$post_count/
  both_time_genus$post_total

# get the top genera for each era
both_time_genus_long <- pivot_longer(both_time_genus[,c(1,6,7)], col = c(2,3))
colnames(both_time_genus_long) <- c("genus", "time", "count")
both_time_genus_long$time <- factor(both_time_genus_long$time,
                                    c("pre_freq", "post_freq"))
top_genera_pre <- head(pre_genomics_genus[order(-pre_genomics_genus$pre_count), ], 10)$genus
top_genera_post <- head(post_genomics_genus[order(-post_genomics_genus$post_count), ], 10)$genus

# reformat to long format for plotting with ggplot
both_time_genus_long_top10 <- both_time_genus_long[order(-both_time_genus_long$count), ]
both_time_genus_long_top10 <- both_time_genus_long_top10[both_time_genus_long_top10$genus %in% unique(c(top_genera_pre, top_genera_post)),]
```
